subject.title: feat: add linux/riscv64 Docker image to multi-platform build

question: Should OpenClaw commit its official Docker release infrastructure and support expectations to linux/riscv64 images now?
rationale: The code shape is bounded, but accepting another official architecture affects release duration, artifact guarantees, dependency support, and ongoing operational ownership; repository evidence does not establish that commitment automatically.

options.title: Sponsor official riscv64 images
options.body: Approve the architecture with a non-blocking build policy and require end-to-end build, manifest, attestation, pull, and useful-run proof before landing.

options.title: Keep community images external
options.body: Document that riscv64 images remain community-maintained until upstream runtime and dependency support becomes routine enough for official releases.

recommendation.title: Sponsor official riscv64 images
recommendation.body: Approve the architecture with a non-blocking build policy and require end-to-end build, manifest, attestation, pull, and useful-run proof before landing.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history places this person closest to Docker release validation, attestations, and runtime-image maintenance.
